# Node.js
> Node.js® is a free, open-source, cross-platform JavaScript runtime for building servers, web apps, CLI tools, and scripts.

The official Node.js website is the primary source for runtime downloads, API documentation, learning materials, release information, and project updates. It also links to contribution workflows, governance resources, and training for the broader Node.js ecosystem.

## Getting Started
- [Learn Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/learn): Entry point for official learning materials, tutorials, and conceptual guides.
- [About Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/about): Overview of the runtime, project goals, governance, and ecosystem context.
- [Download Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download): Download current and LTS Node.js binaries, installers, and source releases.
- [Latest API Docs](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/): Current version API reference for core modules, globals, and runtime behavior.
- [Linux Foundation Training](https://training.linuxfoundation.org/openjs/): Official training and certification resources for Node.js and OpenJS technologies.

## Learn
- [Introduction to Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/getting-started/introduction-to-nodejs): Introductory guide to what Node.js is and how it works.
- [How Much JavaScript Do You Need To Know To Use Node.js?](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/getting-started/how-much-javascript-do-you-need-to-know-to-use-nodejs): Explains the JavaScript knowledge needed before learning Node.js.
- [Differences between Node.js and the Browser](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/getting-started/differences-between-nodejs-and-the-browser): Compares runtime capabilities, APIs, and execution environments.
- [The V8 JavaScript Engine](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/getting-started/the-v8-javascript-engine): Overview of the JavaScript engine powering Node.js execution.
- [Node.js with WebAssembly](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/getting-started/nodejs-with-webassembly): Introductory guide to using WebAssembly modules in Node.js.

## Asynchronous Work and Runtime Behavior
- [Asynchronous flow control](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/asynchronous-work/asynchronous-flow-control): Covers patterns for coordinating asynchronous operations in Node.js.
- [Discover Promises in Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/asynchronous-work/discover-promises-in-nodejs): Explains Promise-based async programming in the Node.js runtime.
- [The Node.js Event Loop](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/asynchronous-work/event-loop-timers-and-nexttick): Detailed explanation of event loop phases, timers, and nextTick.
- [Understanding process.nextTick()](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/asynchronous-work/understanding-processnexttick): Describes scheduling semantics and when to use process.nextTick().
- [Understanding setImmediate()](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/asynchronous-work/understanding-setimmediate): Explains setImmediate behavior relative to timers and microtasks.

## Modules, Packages, and Tooling
- [Node.js Modules](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/modules): Overview of module systems and loading behavior in Node.js.
- [CommonJS modules](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/modules/commonjs-modules): Guide to authoring and using CommonJS modules.
- [ECMAScript modules](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/modules/ecmascript-modules): Reference and guidance for native ES module support.
- [Package manager tips](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/modules/package-manager-tips): Practical guidance for working with npm and package metadata.
- [Publishing a package](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/modules/publishing-a-package): Walkthrough for preparing and publishing packages to npm.
- [How to use Streams](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/modules/how-to-use-streams): Introductory guide to stream-based data processing.
- [ABI Stability](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/modules/abi-stability): Explains ABI stability for native addons and binary compatibility.

## File System, Networking, and Processes
- [Reading files with Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/manipulating-files/reading-files-with-nodejs): Shows how to read files using callback and Promise-based APIs.
- [Writing files with Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/manipulating-files/writing-files-with-nodejs): Covers writing and updating files from Node.js applications.
- [Working with folders in Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/manipulating-files/working-with-folders-in-nodejs): Basic directory creation, traversal, and management techniques.
- [How to work with Different Filesystems](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/manipulating-files/working-with-different-filesystems): Discusses portability concerns across filesystem implementations.
- [Anatomy of an HTTP Transaction](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/modules/anatomy-of-an-http-transaction): Explains request and response handling with the HTTP module.
- [Get HTTP request body data using Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/modules/anatomy-of-an-http-transaction#request-body): Shows how to collect and process incoming request bodies.

## TypeScript and Advanced Topics
- [Running TypeScript code using transpilation](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/typescript/transpile): Explains compiling TypeScript before executing it with Node.js.
- [Running TypeScript code using ts-node](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/typescript/run): Covers executing TypeScript directly during development workflows.
- [Using the Fetch API with Undici in Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/getting-started/fetch): Guide to HTTP requests using the built-in Fetch API.
- [Backpressuring in Streams](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/modules/backpressuring-in-streams): Explains stream backpressure and flow control for efficient I/O.
- [Diagnostics Channel](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/diagnostics_channel.html): API reference for publishing and subscribing to diagnostic events.
- [Worker Threads](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/worker_threads.html): API reference for multithreaded JavaScript execution in Node.js.

## API Reference
- [API Index](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/): Index of all core Node.js API reference documentation.
- [Globals](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/globals.html): Reference for built-in global objects and web-compatible APIs.
- [Buffer](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/buffer.html): Binary data handling API for byte arrays and encodings.
- [File System](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/fs.html): Reference for filesystem operations, streams, and file handles.
- [HTTP](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/http.html): Core HTTP server and client APIs.
- [Path](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/path.html): Utilities for working with filesystem paths across platforms.
- [Process](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/process.html): Runtime process information, signals, environment, and lifecycle hooks.
- [Stream](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/stream.html): Core stream abstractions for readable, writable, duplex, and transform flows.

## CLI and Runtime Reference
- [Command-line options](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/cli.html): Reference for Node.js CLI flags, environment variables, and runtime options.
- [Environment Variables](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/environment_variables.html): Documents environment variables recognized by Node.js and related tooling.
- [Packages](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/packages.html): Reference for package resolution, exports, imports, and module packaging.
- [Modules](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/modules.html): Core reference for the CommonJS module system.
- [ESM](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/esm.html): Detailed reference for ECMAScript module behavior in Node.js.
- [N-API](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/n-api.html): Stable C API for building native addons across Node.js versions.

## Releases and Downloads
- [Download Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download): Main download page for installers, binaries, and source archives.
- [Previous Releases](https://nodejs.org/en/download/releases/): Archive of historical Node.js release downloads and metadata.
- [Release Schedule](https://nodejs.org/en/about/releases/): Official release lifecycle and support schedule for Node.js versions.
- [Nightly Builds](https://nodejs.org/download/nightly/): Automated nightly build artifacts for testing upcoming changes.
- [Canary Builds](https://nodejs.org/download/v8-canary/): Experimental builds tracking newer V8 integrations and runtime changes.
- [Source Code](https://nodejs.org/en/download/source-code): Source distribution downloads for building Node.js from source.

## Blog and Security
- [Node.js Blog](https://nodejs.org/en/blog): Official announcements, release posts, and project updates.
- [Security Releases](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability): Security advisories and coordinated vulnerability release posts.
- [Release Announcements](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release): Posts covering new Node.js version releases and notable changes.
- [Community Updates](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/community): News about events, initiatives, and ecosystem activity.
- [Project News](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/announcements): General announcements from the Node.js project.
- [Security Policy](https://github.com/nodejs/node/security/policy): Vulnerability reporting process and security handling guidelines.

## Contributing and Project Governance
- [Contributing to Node.js](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): Main contributor guide for code, issues, and pull requests.
- [Node.js on GitHub](https://github.com/nodejs/node): Source repository for the Node.js runtime and project development.
- [About the Node.js Project](https://nodejs.org/en/about): Overview of governance, mission, and project structure.
- [Governance](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md): Governance model, roles, and decision-making processes.
- [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/nodejs/admin/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md): Community behavior expectations and reporting guidance.
- [Collaborator Guide](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/COLLABORATOR_GUIDE.md): Responsibilities and workflows for Node.js collaborators.
- [Build Working Group](https://github.com/nodejs/build): Infrastructure and build system working group repository.
